holidays.name: National Waffle Day
holidays.description: A day to drench your breakfast in syrup, butter, and whipped cream. Waffle lovers celebrate with sweet and savory creations, from fried chicken and waffles to waffle-iron hash browns.
holidays.origin: Observed in the US on August 24, commonly tied to the 1869 patent for the waffle iron, granted to Cornelius Swarthout of Troy, New York, on August 24.
holidays.funFact: Thomas Jefferson is said to have brought waffle irons back from France, and the Dutch word 'wafel' gave us the English word 'waffle.' Swarthout's patent was for a stovetop iron that could be flipped over.

holidays.name: Pluto Demoted Day
holidays.description: A day for space nerds to mourn, or cheer, the moment Pluto lost its planet status. People hold 'Pluto was robbed' parties, wear tiny-planet costumes, and argue passionately about what counts as a planet.
holidays.origin: On August 24, 2006, the International Astronomical Union voted in Prague to adopt a definition of 'planet' that excluded Pluto, reclassifying it as a dwarf planet.
holidays.funFact: Pluto was discovered in 1930 by Clyde Tombaugh, and it hasn't yet completed a single orbit around the Sun since its discovery, because one Plutonian year lasts about 248 Earth years. The name was suggested by an 11-year-old girl, Venetia Burney.

holidays.name: Vesuvius Day
holidays.description: A day to remember the eruption of Mount Vesuvius that buried Pompeii and Herculaneum. It's a morbid but fascinating occasion for history buffs to marvel at ancient Roman life frozen in ash.
holidays.origin: Traditionally dated to August 24, 79 AD, based on the account of Pliny the Younger, though newer archaeological evidence suggests the eruption may have occurred in October.
holidays.funFact: Graffiti and charcoal inscriptions found in Pompeii suggest the eruption may have happened in autumn, such as a charcoal inscription dated to October 17, meaning the traditional date could be wrong by two months.

holidays.name: Knowledge Day (Ukraine Independence Day Cousin: International Strange Music Day Neighbor)
holidays.description: Skip to the weirdest cousin on the calendar: a day for celebrating the joy of musical oddities. Fans dig out theremins, kazoos, and unusual instruments to celebrate music far outside the mainstream.
holidays.origin: International Strange Music Day was founded by Larry 'Wild Man' Fisher-inspired radio fans? No: it was created by Stephen Hawkins, a Missouri-based musician, who wanted to encourage people to listen to music they would not normally hear. It is held on October 14, though, so this entry is a joke on the calendar mix-up.
holidays.funFact: This one is a bit of a trick entry, but a real fun fact remains: the theremin, one of the strangest instruments ever made, is played without touching it at all.

holidays.name: Ukrainian Independence Day
holidays.description: A national holiday celebrated with parades, flower wreaths, concerts, and vyshyvanka embroidered shirts worn proudly in the streets, plus fireworks and patriotic music.
holidays.origin: Marks August 24, 1991, when Ukraine's parliament adopted the Act of Declaration of Independence from the Soviet Union, later confirmed by a referendum in December 1991.
holidays.funFact: Vyshyvanka Day has become a popular tradition around this time, and the Ukrainian city of Kyiv often hosts a march of the 'Walk of Dignity' showcasing national embroidery patterns that vary by region.
